# TypeScript SDK

The functions a film imports from `"turbomotion"`, taken from the doc comments on the exports in `crates/script/sdk`. Only documented exports are listed.

## `comp`

The film: size, frame rate, layers, and the edit timeline of shots, transitions, overlays and hits.

```ts
export class Shot
```
A shot of the edit timeline, built by `shot()`.

```ts
export const shot = (opts: ShotOpts): Shot
```
One shot of the edit: its layers, how it comes in (`in`), a 2D `move`, a 3D `camera` move.

```ts
export class Film
```
A composition being built: add layers, shots, audio and markers, and it becomes the JSON the engine renders.

```ts
export const comp = (opts: CompOpts): Film
```
The film: `comp({ width, height, fps, bg, ... })`, then `film.add(layers)`, `film.shot(...)` and `export default film`.

## `components/barRace`

Horizontal bars that grow to their values, each with a label on the left and a counter riding its tip.

```ts
export function barRace(o: BarRaceOpts): Part
```
`barRace({ tl, at: 37, dur: 2.4, bars: [{ label: "turbomotion", value: 373, color: "#ff5a1f" }, ...] })`.

## `components/bboxOverlay`

HUD bounding boxes with mono labels (`name · 1240×180 · ok`). A box has a state (ok / clash / fixed) shown in a token colour, and may change state and move at a later time (a clash that is fixed).

```ts
export const stateColor = (th: Theme, s: BoxState): string
```
Box colours: ok = cobalt, clash = turbo (the red of this palette), fixed = volt.

```ts
export function bboxOverlay(o: BboxOverlayOpts): Part
```
`bboxOverlay({ tl, at: 1, boxes: [{ x: 120, y: 80, w: 1240, h: 180, label: "title" }] })`; `x`,`y` are the top-left.

## `components/browserWindow`

A generic browser window: three dots, a URL pill, a spinner and a skeleton page. No real brand marks.

```ts
export function browserWindow(o: BrowserWindowOpts): Part
```
`browserWindow({ tl, url: "localhost:3000", at: 0.4 })`: `root` is the group to move or break apart.

## `components/cardWall`

A tilted wall of coloured 3D cards that pops in from the centre, with a hero card the camera can dolly toward. The wall's origin is the hero card, so a camera aimed at the wall is aimed at the hero.

```ts
export function cardWall(o: CardWallOpts): Part
```
`cardWall({ tl, cols: 8, rows: 5, seed: 11, hero: 20, at: 0.1 })`: `wall` is the parent, `hero` the hero card layer.

## `components/codePanel`

A mono code panel: syntax colours (as text `runs`), a highlight bar that moves to the current line, and lines that are typed or revealed one per `perLine` seconds with a `tick` each.

```ts
export function highlight(line: string, c: Record<string, string>): TextRun[]
```
Syntax `runs` for one line of TypeScript-like code.

```ts
export function codePanel(o: CodePanelOpts): Part
```
`codePanel({ tl, at: 12.5, perLine: 1, lines: ["const film = comp({ ... });", ...] })`.

## `components/cutout`

A cut-out subject that is alive: a picture (or any layer) standing on the ground with a contact shadow, moving by itself. Idle motion is a looping expression on the *body*, so the group around it stays free for the film's own moves (a stage glides the group between poses, a timeline enters it) and the two never fight over one property.  const hand = cutout({ id: "hand", src: "assets/hand.png", size: [300, 290], pivot: "base", idle: { float: { amp: 12, period: 3.2 }, sway: { deg: 3, period: 4.1 } }, shadow: { width: 260, y: 150 }, ring: { rx: 230 } }); shot({ layers: [hand] });                 // pos, scale, rotation and opacity of `hand.root` are yours to move

```ts
export interface Wave
```
A looping wave: one full cycle every `period` seconds, offset by `phase` (0..1 of a cycle).

```ts
export interface CutoutOpts
```
Options for `cutout`: an image or built layer that lives by itself (float, sway, breathe, drift, tilt).

```ts
export function cutout(o: CutoutOpts): Part
```
`cutout({ id, src, size, idle, shadow, ring })`: `root` is the group to place and move; `body` is the picture.

## `components/promptBox`

A glass prompt card with a typed command: mono text, a caret that follows the typed end and blinks on beats, a `type` sound per character and an optional Enter (the card presses on a spring; the caret becomes a dot you can swell).

```ts
export function promptBox(o: PromptBoxOpts): Part
```
`promptBox({ tl, text: "turbomotion render launch.ts", at: 0.9, cps: 14, enterAt: 3.2 })`.

A hand-drawn strike-through: a jittered zigzag path drawn on with `trim`, with a `glitch` on the first stroke.

```ts
export function scribble(o: ScribbleOpts): Part
```
`scribble({ tl, at: 1.2, pos: [960, 560], w: 1300, h: 760 })`: `shape` is the layer; the path overshoots the box slightly.

## `components/statCounter`

A big number that counts up and slams: it lands with a scale overshoot and a `stamp`, a small mono label under it.

```ts
export function statCounter(o: StatCounterOpts): Part
```
`statCounter({ tl, value: 373, suffix: " fps", label: "frames per second", at: 36 })`.

## `components/textStack`

A stack of words that arrive on cue and lay themselves out. Rows grow downward (or upward from a bottom edge), a row that gets too wide wraps, and a centred row re-centres as words join it. Every position comes from the renderer's own text shaping, and words already on screen glide to their new place (a FLIP reflow) instead of jumping.

```ts
export interface StackRole
```
How one kind of word looks and enters.

```ts
export interface TextStackOpts
```
Options for `textStack`: lines of text that reflow (FLIP) as items are added, removed or reordered.

```ts
export function textStack(o: TextStackOpts): Part
```
`textStack({ tl, items, roles, pos: [90, 120], width: 560 })`. Returns the word layers in `words` (item order).

## `components/title3d`

A 3D word that tumbles in letter by letter: `letters3d` plus the launch film's entrance (stagger, back.out) as one call.

```ts
export function title3d(word: string, o: Title3DOpts): Part
```
`title3d("MOTION", { tl, at: 0.3, size: 240 })`: `letters` are the layers, `end` is when the last one has landed.

## `film-types`

```ts
export interface Hit
```
A sound on a moment. `at` is film time (a number, or a literal like `"title.start+0.8"`); inside `shot({ hits })` it is shot-local seconds.

## `layers`

Layers as builders. A layer holds its static properties and the tweens a timeline attached to it; `toJSON()` turns both into one composition layer.

```ts
export class Layer
```
A layer of any kind as a builder: its properties plus the tweens a timeline attached to it.

```ts
export function list(items: unknown, where = "layers"): Layer[]
```
The top-level layers in `items` (arrays are opened; groups stay whole).

```ts
export const flatten = (items: unknown, where = "layers"): Layer[]
```
Every layer in `items`, groups opened so children follow their parent.

```ts
export const text = (content: string | CounterSpec, o: TextOpts = {}): Layer
```
A text layer: `text("Hello", { size, font, weight, color, pos, preset })`. Also takes a counter `{ from, to, dur }`.

```ts
export const solid = (color: Color, o: SolidOpts = {}): Layer
```
A flat rectangle: backgrounds, flashes, mattes.

```ts
export const image = (src: string, o: ImageOpts = {}): Layer
```
A picture: `image("photo.jpg", { fit, focus, camera, parallax })`.

```ts
export const shape = (items: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, o: ShapeOpts = {}): Layer
```
A vector shape from raw items: `{rect: [x, y, w, h], radius, fill, stroke}`, `{ellipse: [...]}`, `{d: "M..."}`.

```ts
export function rect(w: number, h: number, o: RectOpts = {}): Layer
```
A rectangle centred on its position, optionally rounded: `rect(260, 340, { fill: "#ff6b3d", radius: 18 })`.

```ts
export function group(o: LayerOpts = {}, children: unknown = []): Layer
```
An invisible handle: parent layers to it to move, scale or rotate them as one.

```ts
export const camera = (o: CameraOpts = {}): Layer
```
A 3D camera: `camera({ pos, poi, zoom, dof })`. Shots with 3D layers and no camera get a default one.

```ts
export const raw = (spec: Record<string, unknown>): Layer
```
Escape hatch: any layer the engine knows, as written in `turbomotion comp catalogue`.

## `measure`

Layout with the exact font shaping used by the composition renderer.

```ts
export function configureMeasure(roles: Record<string, string> = {}, directory = ""): void
```
Called by comp() so font roles and relative files agree with the film.

```ts
export function measure(text: string, options: MeasureOptions = {}): Measured
```
Pixel dimensions and character/word boxes, using the most recently constructed comp's fonts.

## `motion`

Small deterministic helpers: seeded random numbers, ranges, interpolation, grids.

```ts
export function rand(seed: number): Rand
```
A seeded generator (mulberry32). The same seed always gives the same numbers, on every machine.

```ts
export function grid(cols: number, rows: number, cell: number | [number, number]): Cell[]
```
`cols` x `rows` cells of size `cell` (a number, or [width, height]), row by row, centred on the origin.

```ts
export function darken(color: string, amount = 0.55): string
```
Darken a `#rrggbb` colour by `amount` (0..1); other colour forms come back unchanged.

## `overwrite`

Interrupted properties retain their exact easing via the engine's scalar expression form.

```ts
export function overwritten(tweens: Tween[], base: Value | undefined, id: string, prop: string): unknown
```
Compile only when an author opts into overwrite; the ordinary key/tween path remains compact.

## `sound`

Sound: audio layers, and hits (sound-kit cues placed on moments). Hits made on a timeline are shot-local seconds; `film.timeline` turns them into the engine's `"<shotId>.start+<t>"` literal, so the engine, which knows where each shot really starts once transitions overlap, puts them on the right frame.

```ts
export function audio(src: string, o: AudioOpts = {}): Layer
```
A sound on the timeline: `audio("launch/music/bed.wav", { id: "music", volume: 0.8, fade_out: 1 })`.

```ts
export const hit = (at: number | string, cue: string, volume?: number): Hit
```
A hit at film time: `hit(26, "boom")` or `hit("drop.start+0.2", "riser", 0.5)`.

```ts
export function inShot(id: string, hits: Hit[] = []): Hit[]
```
Shot-local hits as film-time literals: `at: 0.8` in shot "deep" becomes `"deep.start+0.8"`.

## `stage`

Smart animate. Describe where each named layer sits in a few poses, then glide between poses: the layers are matched by name, only the properties that differ are tweened, and every layer lands on the same clock. This is what makes a scene feel like one object changing rather than one picture replacing another.  const s = stage({ title, clock }, { start: { title: { x: 360, y: 300, opacity: 0 }, clock: { x: 360, y: 800, scale: 0.6 } }, shown: { title: { opacity: 1 }, clock: { y: 640, scale: 1 } }, }).start("start"); s.go(tl, "shown", { at: 0.4, dur: 0.7, ease: "expo.out", stagger: 0.06 });  A layer a pose does not mention keeps its place. To make one disappear, give it `opacity: 0`. A group's opacity reaches everything parented to it (the engine's null layers do not pass opacity down, so the stage does).

```ts
export interface Pose
```
The properties a pose can set; the same names `tl.to` animates.

```ts
export class Stage
```
Named poses for layers; `go` tweens between them.

```ts
export const stage = (layers: Record<string, Layer>, poses: Record<string, Record<string, Pose>>): Stage
```
Smart Animate: name poses for a set of layers, then `go("pose", { at, dur })` moves every layer to its new state.

## `three`

Solids. Every 3D object is one `mesh` layer whose `geometry` says what it is made of: glyph outlines, a box, a sphere, a torus, a cylinder or an SVG path pushed into depth. `text3d` and `letters3d` are the text geometry; `spin` turns any of them about its own axis.

```ts
export function mesh(geometry: Geometry, o: MeshOpts = {}): Layer
```
A mesh from any geometry: `mesh({ kind: "sphere", size: 300 }, { color: "#e8402f", pos: [960, 540, 0] })`.

```ts
export const box = (g: Omit<BoxGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A box: `box({ size, height?, depth? }, { color, side, pos, rot_y })`.

```ts
export const sphere = (g: Omit<SphereGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A sphere of diameter `size`.

```ts
export const torus = (g: Omit<TorusGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A ring facing the viewer: outer diameter `size`, band thickness `tube`.

```ts
export const cylinder = (g: Omit<CylinderGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A cylinder of diameter `size` and `height`; `top: 0` makes a cone.

```ts
export const extrude = (g: Omit<ExtrudeGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
An SVG path `d` filled and pushed `depth` deep.

```ts
export function text3d(content: string, o: Text3DOpts = {}): Layer
```
Extruded text: `text3d("Hi", { font, weight, size, depth, bevel, color, side, material, ...layer })`.

```ts
export function letters3d(word: string, o: Letters3DOpts = {}): Layer[]
```
Split `word` into one 3D text layer per letter, centred on `pos` (default the origin: pass your own). Letter boxes come from the renderer's own shaping (`measure`), so kerning and tracking match flat text. Spaces take room but make no layer. Returns the layers in reading order, ready for a staggered tween.

```ts
export function spin(degreesPerSecond: number, from = 0): string
```
A turntable: the angle of a steady turn as an expression, for `rot_y` (or `rot_x` / `rotation`) of a 3D object. `box({ size: 200 }, { rot_y: spin(90) })` makes a full turn in four seconds; `from` is the starting angle.

## `timeline`

A GSAP-style timeline. `tl.to(layer, { rot_y: 0, duration: 0.8 }, 0.2)` records tweens on the layer; when the layer is written out, all tweens on one property merge into one key list in time order.

```ts
export function callSite(): string
```
The first stack frame outside the SDK: the line of the author's script that made this call.

```ts
export class Timeline
```
Tweens placed on a time axis, compiled into each layer's keyframes.

```ts
export const timeline = (defaults: { ease?: Ease; duration?: Seconds } = {}): Timeline
```
A GSAP-style timeline: `tl.to(layer, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5 }, at)`, `from`, `set`, with `stagger` and `overwrite`.

```ts
export function compileTweens(out: Record<string, any>, tweens: Tween[], id: string): void
```
Write the tweens of one layer into `out` (the layer's JSON): one merged property per animated name.

## `tween-types`

```ts
export interface Animatable
```
Properties a tween can animate. `x`/`y`/`z` move `pos`.

## `types`

Shared types. Everything an author can write is described here, so an editor catches mistakes before the render does.

```ts
export type Prop<T = number> = T | string | { [key: string]: unknown };
```
A property: a constant, an expression string, or any raw form the engine accepts (tween, keys, loop).

```ts
export interface LayerOpts
```
What every layer takes. `x`, `y`, `z` are shorthand for `pos`.

```ts
export interface CounterSpec
```
`text` may also be a counter that counts from `from` to `to`.

```ts
export interface TorusGeometry { kind: "torus"; size: number; tube?: number }
```
A ring facing the viewer: `size` is the outer diameter, `tube` the band's thickness (a quarter of `size`).

```ts
export interface CylinderGeometry { kind: "cylinder"; size: number; height: number; top?: number }
```
`top` is the top diameter (0 makes a cone).

```ts
export interface ExtrudeGeometry { kind: "extrude"; d: string; size: number; depth?: number; bevel?: number }
```
An SVG path `d` (filled) scaled to `size` wide and pushed `depth` deep (0.3 x size when left out).
